fichas.title: Drawings and levels of abstraction
fichas.summary: Architectural drawings abstract reality in two dimensions. Their degree of abstraction depends on their content and intended purpose: perspectives, collages and renderings approximate reality, diagrams explain functional interactions, and working drawings communicate the dimensions, materials and arrangement needed for production with unambiguous detail.

fichas.title: Computer-aided drawings
fichas.summary: Computer-aided drawing uses raster graphics, which save pixels, and vector graphics, which save drawing elements and their properties. CAD commonly uses three-dimensional, object-oriented data models to generate output views. Drawing elements can be linked to database information such as layer, material and manufacturing data; volume models can also support building simulations and three-dimensional input and output.
uses: Linking drawing elements to additional information
Supporting structural, acoustic, climatic and lighting investigations

fichas.title: CAD drawing layers and layer naming
fichas.summary: A CAD drawing can be structured by arranging similar objects on separate layers, including text, dimensions, furniture, openings, construction, and title-block information. The illustrated naming convention uses author, categorisation and description fields separated by underscores. Names should be understandable, avoid special characters, and communicate their content within the character limits described. ISO 13567 is also identified as a standard governing layer naming.
uses: Naming layers for clear communication and data exchange
